Short answer
- Target a modern LED adjustable task lamp with tunable color temperature, dimming, and low wattage (high lumens-per-watt). From our catalog memory, the Meadowlight Lamp is a candidate, but I don’t have full spec sheets in memory — key claims below need verification before purchase.

What I found in the catalog memory
- Meadowlight Lamp — listed under “desk lamp / task lamps / lighting products” and appears to be an adjustable desk lamp.
- Several generic entries for “adjustable desk lamps,” “desk lamp,” and “task lamps.”

Evidence available and limits
- Evidence: the catalog contains a Meadowlight Lamp product entry and multiple lamp-type product entries. That indicates these items exist in the catalog.
- Missing/unknown: the memory does not contain product specifications (wattage, lumens, CRI, color temperature range, ENERGY STAR or other efficiency certification, dimming or smart features, price, warranty, expected lifetime). Because those specs aren’t available in memory, any specific performance or efficiency claims about these catalog items must be verified from the product pages or spec sheets.

What to look for (recommended minimum specs for an energy-efficient office desk lamp)
- Light source: LED (solid-state) — best lumens/watt and long life.
- Power: around 6–12 W for ~800–1,200 lumens (aim for ~70–100 lm/W or better).
- Brightness: 800–1,200 lumens (task lighting); adjustable/dimmable is strongly recommended.
- Color temperature: tunable 2700–5000 K or at least 3000–4000 K for office work (neutral to cool white).
- Color rendering (CRI): ≥90 for accurate color rendering (important if you view printed materials or colors).
- Dimming: smooth dimming to reduce power when full brightness isn’t needed.
- Controls: easy reach controls, ideally touch or integrated dimmer; optional motion sensor or auto-off timer saves energy.
- Mounting: clamp or weighted base depending on desk and space.
- Certifications: ENERGY STAR or equivalent, and documented lumen maintenance (L70 hours) if available.
- Lifetime/warranty: LED lifetime >=25,000–50,000 hours and at least a 1–3 year warranty.
- Additional: USB charging or integrated cable management can be useful.

Recommendations and how they map to the catalog evidence
- Meadowlight Lamp — recommend as a candidate to review because it appears in the catalog as an adjustable desk/task lamp. Required verification: wattage, lumens, CRI, color temperature options, dimming, ENERGY STAR certification (if any), lifetime rating, price, mounting style and warranty.
- If Meadowlight lacks tunable white or high CRI, pick another LED adjustable task lamp that meets the specs above (catalog has multiple “adjustable desk lamps” entries — verify their detailed specs before choosing).

Claims that require verification (you should request or check these on product pages)
- Exact power consumption (W).
- Delivered lumens (not just bulb equivalence).
- Lumens per watt (efficiency).
- Color temperature range and CRI.
- Whether the lamp is dimmable and what type of dimmer/control it uses.
- ENERGY STAR or other efficiency certification.
- Expected LED lifetime (L70 value) and warranty duration.
- Compatibility with smart home hubs (if wanted).
- Physical mounting (clamp vs. base) and dimensions to ensure fit on your desk.
- Price and availability.

If you want, I can
- Pull full product specs and prices for the Meadowlight Lamp and other catalog desk lamps (I’ll verify wattage, lumens, CRI, color temp, dimming, certifications, lifetime, and warranty).
- Give a short list of 2–3 specific models (from the catalog) that best match your budget and desk style once you confirm your preferences.

Quick questions to narrow choices
- Budget range?
- Preference for clamp vs. base?
- Do you want tunable white (warm to cool) or is a single color temp fine?
- Need USB charging or smart-home integration?
- Desk size / ceiling height / any glare/reflection concerns?

Tell me how you want to proceed and I’ll fetch the detailed specs and make a final recommendation.
